content_voiceover: This diagnostic algorithm is the board-favorite approach to Castleman disease. It starts with Castleman-like lymph node histology on biopsy, which by itself isn't diagnostic, you must first exclude other disease-associated causes, and the slide groups these into three buckets worth memorizing: infectious causes like EBV, mycobacteria, toxoplasmosis, and CMV; autoimmune and inflammatory causes like IgG4-related disease, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and adult-onset Still's disease; and neoplastic mimics like Kaposi sarcoma, mantle or marginal zone lymphoma, and germinotropic lymphoproliferative disorder. Once those are excluded, CT with or without PET defines the distribution and guides further biopsy, splitting patients into unicentric Castleman disease, a single nodal region, versus multicentric Castleman disease, multiple regions. Multicentric disease then branches three ways based on etiology: HHV-8-associated MCD, typically in HIV-positive or immunocompromised patients; POEMS-associated MCD, tied to the polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, M protein, skin changes syndrome; and idiopathic MCD, or iMCD, when HHV-8 and POEMS are both ruled out. iMCD then splits further into iMCD-NOS and iMCD-TAFRO, the latter being the aggressive variant with thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, reticulin fibrosis, and organomegaly, a distinction that matters a lot for prognosis and urgency of treatment.
keypoints: Castleman-like histology is nonspecific; must exclude infectious, autoimmune/inflammatory, and neoplastic mimics first
CT plus or minus PET defines distribution, splitting unicentric (UCD) from multicentric (MCD)
MCD subtypes: HHV8-MCD, POEMS-MCD, and idiopathic MCD (iMCD)
iMCD splits into iMCD-NOS and iMCD-TAFRO (thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, reticulin fibrosis, organomegaly)
TAFRO is the aggressive, high-mortality iMCD variant
keypoint_voiceover: The algorithm in three steps. First, Castleman-like histology needs exclusion of infectious, autoimmune, and neoplastic mimics before you call it Castleman disease. Second, imaging distribution splits unicentric from multicentric disease. Third, multicentric disease branches into HHV-8-associated, POEMS-associated, or idiopathic, and idiopathic MCD further splits into NOS and the aggressive TAFRO variant, which stands for thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, reticulin fibrosis, and organomegaly.
